subject: Monthly metrics: Signals & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: simon.lee@acme.com, contracts@acme.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Monthly metrics: Signals & next steps

Team / Simon — attaching the November KPI package (dashboard + raw latency exports). Quick summary up top and asks below. Please review before Monday's QBR prep session.

Key signals (top-level):
- 95th pct latency for text-generation up 18% month-over-month (peak windows 10:00–13:00 PST) — correlated with a 22% increase in concurrent hosted requests.
- Unit inference cost per 1K tokens increased ~7% due to higher long-context usage and more frequent small-batch bursts.
- Uptime: 99.98% for hosted endpoints; two brief region failovers (eu-west-1) triggered automatic fallback — no customer impact reported but increased error budget usage.
- Usage: enterprise sandbox accounts are spiking (Acme included) with heavy long-sequence embedding jobs.

Asks:
1) Marcus — can you validate whether any committed Dedicated pools are saturated or if routing changes caused the burst into hosted capacity? Flag any customer traffic shaping we should run.
2) Laura — please triage the latency trend CSV and call out any model-version regressions or quantization differences; highlight top 3 potential mitigations (cache tuning, batching policy tweaks, kernel config).
3) Evelyn — can you prepare a one-slide SLO escalation recommendation if 95th stays above our target next week (include cost delta for temporary extra capacity)?
4) Simon / Acme — FYI: you may see longer tail latencies for those long-context embedding runs; we've attached the raw export and will propose mitigations in the QBR.

Attachments: [Attachment: kpi-nov-2026-dashboard.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)], [Attachment: latency-trend-agg.csv (CSV, 220KB)]

Thanks — want to go into the QBR with concrete options, not just data dumps.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Lead, Enterprise GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, simon.lee@acme.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Monthly metrics: Signals & next steps

Thanks Ben — reviewed the latency CSV quickly. Initial notes:
- The jump maps to model: open-6b-v2 @ v2.1.0 on the dedicated pool at 10:12 PST (see spike at 10:15 in the CSV). Might be a kernel fallback happening on a subset of hosts.
- Top tokens-per-request quartile shows a shift from median 1.2k to 3.8k for enterprise sandbox traffic (Acme included). That explains the cost bump.

Quick mitigations I recommend for the QBR deck (draft):
- Short term (24–72h): prioritize prefix caching + raise continuous batching window for the affected pools; temporarily increase batch timeout to absorb bursts.
- Mid term (2–4 weeks): enable quantization profile Q3 for long-context-heavy models in sandbox pools; instrument per-request trace to confirm kernel selection.
- Customer communication: we should notify top-5 sandbox users about best-practice prompt trimming + recommend using streaming for interactive flows.

[Quoted text: "Key signals..." from Ben Carter]

I'll flesh out one slide and attach a snippet of a proposed batching policy.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, simon.lee@acme.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Monthly metrics: Signals & next steps

Adding ops context — I pulled Dedicated pool telemetry:
- Two hosts in pool-dedicated-14 reported higher CPU waits and kernel fallbacks at 10:10–10:25 PST; autoscaler held steady but pods were queuing. No sustained OOMs.
- Routing policy temporarily shifted approx 9% of long-run requests to hosted due to a recently enabled capacity-smoothing rule (we rolled this week).

Action items I recommend (for Monday):
- Revert the capacity-smoothing rule for affected pools until batching/quant profiles are applied (ops can do this rollback with zero downtime).
- Approve temporary burst capacity (extra 2 GPUs on pool-dedicated-14) for 72 hours to burn down queued KV caches and observe 95th latency impact. Estimate incremental cost: $4.8K/day — I'll itemize in the SLO doc.
- Triage: ops will add enhanced kernel selection logging for that pool (30m change window).

[Attachment: slo-escalation-proposal.docx (DOCX, 48KB)]

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: simon.lee@acme.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Bcc: contracts@acme.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 15:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Monthly metrics: Signals & next steps

Thanks all — summary / decisions for QBR prep: 
- Immediate: Marcus to revert capacity-smoothing rule and apply temporary +2 GPU burst to pool-dedicated-14 (72h). Marcus to confirm cost line in SLO doc; Evelyn to fold cost into the escalation slide.
- Laura to draft the one-slide mitigation proposals (short/mid-term) and include concrete numbers (expected p95 improvement, rough cost delta).
- Ben to prepare customer-facing note for Acme: short explanation + recommended prompt trims and guidance for streaming vs batch; will share draft by EOD Sunday.

Simon — appreciate the patience. We'll include a short customer-facing appendix in the QBR with recommended config changes for Acme sandbox workloads; if you want a quick 15-min sync Sunday afternoon I can do it.

Next steps: everyone, please upload final slide/notes to the Drive link by 08:00 PST Monday. I'll consolidate into the QBR deck.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Lead, Enterprise GTM
Redwood Inference
